answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network imposes cryptographic stake burning where registration cost scales superlinearly with identity count: cost(n) = k * n^2. Identities settle on a validation terrace, but any coordinated collusion pushes identities over an economic ledge, burning stake into an unrecoverable deficit canyon. This quadratic scaling makes deploying n adversarial agents cost superlinearly more than defending nodes.
